Injured in a car accident? A former insurance company trial attorney fights for full compensation for medical bills, lost wages, and pain. No fee unless we win: 323-452-5222.

Hurt in a Car Accident? The Insurance Company Already Has a Plan.

Within hours of a crash, the at-fault driver's insurance company opens a file, assigns an adjuster, and sets a reserve, an internal estimate of what your claim might cost. Their goal is to close your claim for as little as possible.

Attorney Vardan Daldumyan knows this process from the inside. Before founding Prospect Law Group, he worked as an in-house trial attorney for an insurance company. Now he uses that experience to build claims the insurance company cannot afford to underpay.

No fee unless we recover. Free consultation, 24/7.

What We Do for You

  1. Handle every call with the insurance companies so you can focus on recovery
  2. Preserve evidence: photos, video, vehicle data, witness statements, and police reports
  3. Get your medical care documented properly, which is what drives claim value
  4. Calculate the full value of your claim, including future medical care and lost earning capacity
  5. Negotiate from strength, and file suit when an insurer will not be reasonable

Compensation You May Recover

  • Medical bills, past and future
  • Lost wages and loss of earning capacity
  • Pain and suffering and emotional distress
  • Vehicle repair or replacement and rental costs
  • Loss of enjoyment of life
  • In wrongful death cases, losses suffered by the family

California Rules That Affect Your Claim

  • Deadline: two years for injury lawsuits, three years for property damage, six months for claims against a government agency
  • Comparative fault: you can recover even if partly at fault, reduced by your share
  • Proposition 213: uninsured drivers generally cannot recover pain and suffering damages from an insured at-fault driver, with some exceptions
  • Minimum insurance: California's minimum liability limits increased in 2025 to $30,000 per person, $60,000 per accident, and $15,000 for property damage. Many drivers carry only the minimum, which is why your own uninsured and underinsured coverage matters.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long do I have to file a car accident claim in California?

Generally two years from the accident for injury claims and three years for property damage. If a government vehicle or road condition was involved, a written claim must be filed within six months.

What if I was partly at fault?

California uses pure comparative fault. You can still recover, reduced by your percentage of fault. If you were 20% at fault, you can recover 80% of your damages.

Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?

Not before talking to a lawyer. Recorded statements are used to find inconsistencies and reduce the value of your claim.

What if the other driver has no insurance?

Your own uninsured motorist coverage may pay for your injuries. We help you make that claim and deal with your insurer.
